newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open little changed Monday as dealers expect the market to continue to trade sideways amid a dearth of market-moving news.

New York arabica futures ended mixed in quiet dealings Friday. September settled 0.35 cent lower at 179.50 cents a lb after ranging from 183.50 to 177.50. Spot July finished up 3.05 at 198.95, while the outer months closed up 0.45 to down 3.25.
The July/September switch widened to 19.45 cents at the close from 16.05 cents Thursday.

Technically, traders pegged September resistance at 185.00 cents, with the next upside target at 192.00 cents. Near-term support was seen at 175.00 cents, followed by September's low set Thursday of 168.75.

On the weather front, no damaging cold is indicated this week in Brazil's coffee belt, although temperatures may turn cooler in the southern growing areas on Saturday or Sunday. But no significant cold is indicated, U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Monday.
There may be some disruptions and delays to the Brazil harvest due to very wet weather this month, WSC added.
After Friday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks were unchanged as of June 19, to 47,325 bags. There were 1,600 bags pending grading, the exchange said.

CFTC's Commitment of Traders report released late Friday showed non-commercial long positions in the two weeks ended June 17 fell by 2,821 lots, to 4,379 lots. Non-commercial short positions fell by 810 lots, to 837 lots.
Commercial long positions in the two weeks rose by 420 lots, to 7,538 lots, while commercial short positions fell by 3,292 lots, to 13,191 lots.
Nonreportable longs positions decreased by 2,980 lots, to 9,303 lots and nonreportable short positions declined by 1,282 lots, tp 7,192 lots.
In London, robusta futures drifted lower early Monday in thin trading. At the midday break, benchmark LIFFE September was down $20, to $1,840, while spot July fell $17, to $1,823.
